newsitem.title: USA: TI introduces chip for higher speed modems. [CORRECTED 20:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: TI introduces chip for higher speed modems. [CORRECTED 20:30 GMT]

text.p: Texas Instruments Inc said it "introduced" a new higher speed version of its digital signal processor chip for use in a variety of emerging communication technologies like cable modem and digital subscriber line systems (corrects from "with U.S. Robotics Corp's soon-to-be released 56-kilobit modem technology").
A Texas Instruments spokeswoman said the new chip is now sampling in limited quantities and that volume production is expected to begin in the second half of 1997.

Texas Instruments said the chip can process 1.6 billion instructions per second. It said a file that takes 10 minutes to transmit using standard delivery methods via the Internet would take less than five seconds.

Texas Instruments said its new chip, the TMS320C6201, is 10 times faster than currently commercially available digital signal processors, or DSPs, the specialized semiconductor designed for the fast, math-intensive computing required by modems.

DSPs are the basic hardware used not only in modems, but other consumer electronic products including cellular phones, pagers, hard disk drives, digital satellite systems and audio/video equipment. TI holds 45 percent share of the global DSP market.
"Texas Instruments' new technology will enable us to continue leading the revolution in Internet access," said Dale Walsh, vice president of Advanced Development, U.S. Robotics.

"With this chip, not only will more users be able to log on to the Internet, but they will also be able to download files 120 times faster than today," Walsh said, adding that, "The World Wide Web will no longer be the World Wide Wait."
The company said it plans to hold a conference call about its plans for the chip at 1000 CST/1600 GMT with John Scarisbrick, a senior vice president at Texas Instruments Semiconductor Group.
